os: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS under WSL2, kernel 5.15.167.4-microsoft-standard-WSL2, Windows host

hardware.wsl_view: 12 cores x 2 SMT threads = 24 logical CPUs (siblings 2k, 2k+1)
hardware.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti, compute capability 8.9, 12282 MiB
hardware.host_cpu_topology: 8 performance cores (SMT) + 16 efficient cores, 32 logical CPUs; the Windows host schedules the 24 WSL2 vCPUs

binding.mapping: rank i uses logical CPUs 2i and 2i+1, the two SMT siblings of WSL core i
binding.upstream: I_MPI_PIN=1, I_MPI_PIN_DOMAIN with the explicit masks below

protocol.order: S, sidia333_nc_cluster, cghelgeo, L; GPU then fork CPU then upstream for each
protocol.GPU_MPS_reason: NVIDIA MPS is supported on Linux and QNX only. Under WSL2 the GPU is driven by the Windows driver through /dev/dxg; its WSL libcuda has no MPS client and nvidia-cuda-mps-control exits with status 33 on start, while the native Linux 595.99.02 user-space driver cannot open /dev/nvidiactl (ENXIO).
protocol.suite_time_metric: sum of native per-case runtest*.result elapsed times (one native -runtest* job per route)
protocol.data_source: same fork DFT_DATA19 files for all three configurations (32 inputs, 25 PAO + 19 VPS files)
protocol.ELPA: bundled OpenMP ELPA 2026.02.002; AVX2 kernels at run time (AVX-512 kernels are built but this CPU has no AVX-512)
protocol.wall_metric: guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC duration of the MPI job including the 2 s monitor polling; the guest monotonic clock ran about 10% slow (1.111 external s per guest s), so external_wall_seconds maps start/end through clock-log.csv where the log covers them

clock.finding: The WSL2 guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC advanced 10% less than an external HTTPS Date reference; CLOCK_REALTIME, which omp_get_wtime and therefore OpenMX dtime/Total Computational Time use, is stepped to the host time about every 30 s.
clock.log: clock-log.csv: external (HTTPS Date, 1 s resolution, sampled at a second boundary), guest monotonic, guest realtime, load
clock.consequence: native OpenMX times (omp_get_wtime) agree with the external clock: every MPI job covered by the log ran 1.4-7.6 s longer externally than its native time (start-up, shutdown, work between suite cases). Between steps the realtime clock runs as slowly as the monotonic clock, so a case of a few seconds can read up to about 10% short, or up to about 3.6 s long when it spans a step.
